storage_source: Central Arizona Project Lake Pleasant operations endpoint, the service behind the public Lake Pleasant graphic
capacity_source: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers National Inventory of Dams. CAP publishes a percent of its 1,702-foot maximum and no full level in acre-feet, so ADR-070 does not fire and ADR-003's inventory rule decides the denominator (ADR-104).
selection: One reservoir: Lake Pleasant behind New Waddell Dam, the only Central Arizona Project storage reservoir. The endpoint answers a single current record and holds no history, so the published series begins on the day of admission and grows in the dense-history cache (ADR-104).

capacity.capacity_source: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers National Inventory of Dams

review.why: CAP's LP_PercentFull is measured against the 1,702-foot maximum pool, which back-computes to about 891,840 acre-feet; the inventory's normal storage is 811,784 and its maximum 1,063,163. CAP publishes the percentage and not the acre-foot figure, so there is no operator full level to prefer under ADR-070, and the inventory's normal storage is the denominator. The 891,840 figure is recorded here so a reader of the two percentages knows why they differ (ADR-104).
